itemText: Install a Debug build that points at the Mac's local API address and confirm the phone reaches it.
Write the short how-to for local testing into the iOS README.
Check on the phone that email and password sign-in works against the production API and fix anything that fails.
Show a sign-in screen when no token is saved instead of empty screens with errors.
Add previews with sample data for the Review, Triage, Add and Knowledge screens so they can be restyled without the API.
Rename the course-level wording once the owner picks the new name.
Run the weekly scheduled reinstall once by hand and confirm it works over Wi-Fi with the phone unlocked.
On the Review screen, put the Show Answer button at the bottom of the screen and let a tap anywhere on the card reveal the answer. This makes reviewing one-handed and faster.
Once the answer is shown, tapping the right half of the screen grades the card Good and tapping the left half grades it Bad. Show a faint hint on each half so the owner knows where to tap.

Make the local API refuse to start in development mode unless its database is the local Postgres container, so the Dev iPhone app and the local web app can never touch production by mistake.

On the iPhone Triage screen, show each card as its front, its back and an optional example, then the original source it came from and an optional note, instead of the current mixed card view. The example is a separate part and should not appear to be part of the front or back.

Replace the Triage list on the iPhone with a one-card-at-a-time mode: swiping a card left rejects it and swiping right approves it, with no buttons on the card. A short list of subjects above lets the owner start the session on one subject or on all of them.

In the swipe Triage mode, let the owner tap a card to edit its text before deciding, and show a remaining count plus a clear finished state when no cards are left. Editing is the rare path, so it must not get in the way of swiping.
